title: Array fundamentals
learn: static vs dynamic arrays, indexing O(1), insert/delete O(n), in-place updates, iteration patterns
hook: Arrays are the most asked category in coding interviews, and the follow-up is almost always "can you do it in place?" Knowing why inserting in the middle costs O(n), and how to avoid it, is the whole game.

explain.prompt: An interviewer asks: why is inserting at the front of an array slow, and how would you remove every copy of a value from an array in place?
keyPoints: arrays are contiguous, so indexing is O(1) but inserting or deleting in the middle shifts everything after it: O(n)
deleting inside a loop is O(n) per delete, O(n²) total
a read pointer scans every value and a write pointer marks where the next kept value goes
the write-pointer pass is O(n) time and O(1) extra space
